title: All computer systems down at Meir Medical Center in Kfar Saba; cause not known, The Yeshiva World reports
date_note: The Yeshiva World says the systems went down on Sunday, 22 November, the day of its article; no clock time given.
geo_basis: Meir Medical Center in Kfar Saba, named by The Yeshiva World
summary: The Yeshiva World reports that all computer systems at Meir Medical Center in Kfar Saba went down on Sunday and that the cause was not immediately known. It says the outage raised concerns of a possible cyberattack, though no cause has been confirmed so far. The article quotes no statement from the hospital or the authorities.
plain: An Israeli hospital, Meir Medical Center in Kfar Saba, lost all its computer systems on Sunday, a news site reports. Nobody has said why yet.
exec: A hospital-wide IT outage whose cause has not been confirmed, The Yeshiva World reports.

key_findings: All computer systems at Meir Medical Center in Kfar Saba went down on Sunday
The cause was not immediately known; no cause confirmed
No statement from the hospital, Health Ministry or National Cyber Directorate is quoted

validation.note: One publisher read: The Yeshiva World (22 Nov), which names no source and quotes no official. English and Hebrew searches found no second report and no statement from the hospital, Clalit, the Health Ministry or the National Cyber Directorate. Its headline says officials are probing a possible cyberattack, but the article text only says the outage raised concerns of one.
